biography: Mathieu Jaminet, born in the heart of France's motorsport country, practically grew up on the fumes of racing fuel. His father, a local rally driver, instilled in him a passion for speed from a young age, karting before he could properly reach the pedals. A defining moment came at age 16 during a national karting championship. Down on power, Mathieu drove with a relentless aggression, elbowing his way through the pack to snatch a podium. This raw talent caught the eye of a Porsche scout, leading to a scholarship in their junior program. Now, at 27, he's a rising star in the Porsche 911 RSR GTE program, known for his fearless overtaking maneuvers and unwavering commitment to pushing the car to its absolute limit. While victories have been hard-fought, his potential is undeniable, and many predict a future World Championship title.
drivingStyle: Jaminet's driving style is characterized by an aggressive, never-give-up attitude. He's a late-braking specialist, often diving into corners where others wouldn't dare. His tire management, while improving, can sometimes be a weakness due to his relentless pushing. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest. He has a natural feel for the car's limits, allowing him to extract every last tenth of a second from the Porsche 911 RSR GTE.
rivalries: Alessandro Rossi: A constant thorn in Jaminet's side, Rossi is known for his calculated driving and often blocks Jaminet's aggressive overtaking attempts, leading to heated on-track battles.
Kenji Nakamura: Nakamura, a Japanese driver with a similar aggressive style, is a direct rival for podium positions. Their clashes are often spectacular, marked by daring overtakes and close calls.
Isabelle Dubois: Another Porsche driver, Dubois is a rising star who constantly challenges Jaminet for the top spot within the team, creating an intense internal rivalry.
quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to French techno music at full volume right before entering the car to get himself pumped up.
Has a specific routine of bouncing the car on its suspension three times before every race start.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, and I'll do whatever it takes to get there."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans GTE Pro class in 2022 alongside his teammates. Despite a late-race scare with a mechanical issue, Jaminet drove a flawless final stint, bringing the car home for a memorable victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Daytona in 2021 with only an hour remaining. A momentary lapse in concentration cost him and his team a likely victory, leaving a deep scar of regret.
